item.title: 'Male Bonding': US' Pete Hegseth and Japan's Shinjiro Koizumi in rowing battle, watch video
item.description: US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and Japan's Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi engaged in a morning physical training session at Fort Meyer Army Base. The leaders performed exercises alongside US soldiers, showcasing a commitment to camaraderie and bilateral ties. This event follows a recent drum battle between Japan's PM and South Korea's President, highlighting Japan's effective soft power diplomacy.

item.title: Viral clip shows Youtuber Omi In A Hellcat leaving prison after federal sentencing
item.description: YouTuber Omi In A Hellcat, real name Bill Omar Carrasquillo, has been released from federal custody after serving time for operating an illegal IPTV business. His operation, Gears TV Reloaded, generated millions by distributing pirated content. Carrasquillo pleaded guilty to multiple charges and was sentenced to 66 months in prison, with his assets seized and auctioned.

item.title: 'Secret beekeeper society': Nick Fuentes calls Candace Owens claims wild after Charlie Kirk time travel and future vision talk
item.description: Nick Fuentes criticized Candace Owens after she claimed Charlie Kirk was a time traveler and used ancient technology. Fuentes called her ideas “totally insane” during his livestream. Owens also said Kirk spoke to her in dreams and accused Turning Point USA members of betrayal. The claims have sparked heavy online criticism and debate.

item.title: Kai Cenat clashes with Twitch CEO Dan Clancy after leaked Streamer Awards footage
item.description: A leaked video shows streamer Kai Cenat confronting Twitch CEO Dan Clancy over "Mount Rushmore" comments. Clancy initially placed Cenat on the list but later claimed it was due to a direct request, a statement Cenat branded as contradictory. The footage reignited debates about platform leadership and creator recognition, sparking mixed reactions across the streaming community.

item.title: Is CIA recruiting Chinese spies? Agency shares step-by-step guide in Mandarin
item.description: In an unprecedented move, the CIA has begun rolling out Mandarin-language videos across social media platforms, calling on Chinese citizens to confidentially disclose sensitive information regarding their government. This initiative, equipped with comprehensive guidelines on how to communicate securely, builds on a previous campaign launched last year, reflecting the rising strain in US-China relations.

item.title: IShowSpeed makes streaming history with first-ever live stream inside Egypt’s Great Pyramid
item.description: IShowSpeed made internet history on January 15, 2026, by becoming the first streamer to broadcast live from inside Egypt's Great Pyramid of Giza. This unprecedented event, part of his "Speed Does Africa" tour, captivated audiences with unfiltered drone shots, historical insights, and Speed's genuine reactions, marking a significant evolution in live travel content.

item.title: After 52 years hunting , top expert delivers final verdict on the Loch Ness Monster
item.description: Adrian Shine, who spent over five decades searching for the Loch Ness Monster, now concludes it almost certainly never existed. Applying scientific methods to folklore and sightings, he attributes reports to natural phenomena and visual illusions. Despite the lack of evidence, Shine values the decades of study, gaining insight into the loch, its ecology, and the ways human perception shapes enduring myths.
item.dc:creator: TOI Trending Desk

item.title: Did Donald Trump suffer a stroke? Here’s what the White House said about reports on the president’s health — fact check
item.description: The White House has refuted claims that former President Donald Trump suffered a stroke months ago, dismissing the reports as "BS Fake News." A professor cited video evidence, including shuffling feet and garbled speech, as indicators of a potential left-brain stroke, though the administration asserts Trump is in excellent health.

item.title: ‘Why am I paying taxes?’ Woman slams government over immigration, says child’s learning suffered due to non-English-speaking students
item.description: A mother's viral video criticizing immigration's impact on public education has ignited debate. She voiced concerns that her daughter struggles to learn math in a classroom with many non-English speakers, questioning the value of her tax contributions. Online reactions largely condemned immigration policies, with some suggesting private schooling as a solution.
